draft.title: Changes that disrupt ecosystems
card: The organisms in an ecosystem depend on each other. A change to one population can change many others through the food web.
Removing a species
if a predator is removed, the animals it ate can increase in number and eat more of their own food. If a pollinator is removed, the plants that rely on it may make fewer seeds and fruit.
Clearing habitat
clearing land removes the food, water and shelter that organisms need. Their populations can fall or disappear from the area.
Introduced species
a species brought in from another place, such as the cane toad in Australia, may eat native animals or compete with them. Native populations can fall as a result.
draft.remember: A change to one population can spread through a food web and change many others.

a.q: A disease wipes out the foxes that eat rabbits in a bushland area. What is the most likely first change?
opts: The rabbit population increases
The rabbit population decreases
The grass population increases
The rabbit population stays the same
a.why: Foxes are predators of rabbits. With fewer foxes, fewer rabbits are eaten, so rabbit numbers are likely to rise. Grass is not likely to increase, because more rabbits would eat more of it.
a.clue: Fewer predators means fewer animals being eaten.

b.q: A farmer clears a patch of bush where native bees live. Nearby wildflowers depend on those bees for pollination. What is the most likely effect on the wildflowers?
opts: They make fewer seeds, so their numbers may fall
They make more seeds because they face less competition
They are unaffected, because wind carries their pollen
They are unaffected, because the bees live somewhere else
b.why: Clearing the bush removes the bees' habitat, so fewer bees can pollinate the flowers. With less pollination, the flowers may make fewer seeds. The wildflowers still depend on the bees, so the loss of the bees affects them even though the bees were not the ones cleared.
b.clue: Think about what the flowers need the bees to do.

b.best: They make fewer seeds, so their numbers may fall

problems.detail: The why says 'even though the bees were not the ones cleared', which is muddled. The bees' habitat was cleared, and it is the wildflowers that were not cleared. This could confuse students about what caused the effect.
The right option is the only one with a qualifier ('may'), so it stands out from the other options.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer that matches the card. The why for (b) muddles which thing was not cleared, and the right option in (b) stands out as the only one with 'may'.
